teams.heading: Jack Crowley ruled out for Ireland until the new year
teams.body: Fly-half Jack Crowley will miss the remainder of the year after being sidelined by a lower limb vascular injury. The 26-year-old, who has earned 35 caps for his country, will be unavailable for Ireland’s upcoming autumn series against Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan confirmed the news, stating that “ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority.” Crowley has been out of action since April, having also missed the summer Tests against Australia, Japan, and New Zealand.

teams.heading: Argentina fall to narrow 27-21 defeat against clinical Australian side
teams.body: Argentina suffered a frustrating 27-21 loss to Australia on home soil in Saturday’s Test match. Despite a resilient defensive effort that tested the Wallabies throughout, Australia capitalised on key moments to secure the victory. Los Pumas struggled to contain a mobile Australian pack, with Fraser McReight’s late turnover proving decisive in the closing stages. Australia coach Les Kiss acknowledged the intensity, stating, “That’s Test rugby, isn’t it? We weren’t perfect; neither were they.” Argentina will need to refine their defensive structures.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One settles legal dispute over player registration categories
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has revised its controversial player eligibility rules following a legal challenge from 25 high-profile players. The league admitted that communication regarding the shift was insufficient and will now reclassify players with 30 or more Brave Blossoms caps from Category A-2 to A-1. Furthermore, naturalised players holding citizenship since May 2025 or earlier will remain in the same registration category as Japan-born players, averting the immediate threat of widespread discrimination claims across the professional competition.

lead.why: This legal resolution fundamentally alters the squad composition landscape for Japan Rugby League One clubs moving forward.

teams.heading: New Zealand falls to South Africa as Springboks level the series
teams.body: The All Blacks saw their pursuit of a historic series victory stalled in Cape Town, falling 33-26 to a clinical South African side. Despite a late rally featuring tries from Roigard, McKenzie, Carter, and captain Ardie Savea, the visitors could not overcome a powerful first-half display from the world champions. The result leaves the series squared at 1-1 with two matches remaining. With the next encounter set for Johannesburg, Dave Rennie’s side must now regroup after failing to maintain their momentum from the opening victory.

teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has hit back at All Blacks boss Dave Rennie following complaints regarding the legality of South Africa’s scrum. Erasmus dismissed the criticism as “nonsense” after New Zealand raised grievances with World Rugby ahead of Saturday’s victory in Cape Town. The Springboks head coach insisted his pack is “scrumming through” legally, claiming the visitors are “under pressure” if they feel the need to lobby via the media. South Africa secured a 33-26 win to level the series at 1-1.
